logic_node.action_detail: In patients with hypertension, blood pressure should be controlled in accordance with guideline-directed medical therapy for hypertension to prevent symptomatic HF. Target SBP <130/80 mmHg for those with CVD risk >=10%. SBP goal <120 mmHg decreased incident HF by 38% (SPRINT trial).

source_text: In patients with hypertension, blood pressure should be controlled in accordance with GDMT for hypertension to prevent symptomatic HF.

logic_node.action: Prescribe SGLT2 inhibitor to prevent HF hospitalization
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with type 2 diabetes and either established CVD or at high cardiovascular risk, SGLT2 inhibitors should be used to prevent hospitalizations for HF. Benefit is independent of glucose lowering. Not evaluated in severe renal impairment (eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73 m2).

source_text: In patients with type 2 diabetes and either established CVD or at high cardiovascular risk, SGLT2i should be used to prevent hospitalizations for HF.

logic_node.action_detail: In the general population, healthy lifestyle habits such as regular physical activity, maintaining normal weight, healthy dietary patterns (Mediterranean, DASH diet), and avoiding smoking are helpful to reduce future risk of HF and preserve cardiac structure.

source_text: In the general population, healthy lifestyle habits such as regular physical activity, maintaining normal weight, healthy dietary patterns, and avoiding smoking are helpful to reduce future risk of HF.

logic_node.action: Screen with natriuretic peptide biomarkers and refer to cardiovascular specialist
logic_node.action_detail: For patients at risk of developing HF, natriuretic peptide biomarker-based screening (BNP >=50 pg/mL triggers echocardiography and cardiovascular specialist referral) followed by team-based care optimizing GDMT can be useful to prevent LV dysfunction (systolic or diastolic) or new-onset HF.

source_text: For patients at risk of developing HF, natriuretic peptide biomarker-based screening followed by team-based care, including a cardiovascular specialist optimizing GDMT, can be useful to prevent the development of LV dysfunction or new-onset HF.

logic_node.action: Use validated multivariable risk scores to estimate incident HF risk
logic_node.action_detail: In the general population, validated multivariable risk scores (Framingham Heart Failure Risk Score, Health ABC Heart Failure Score, ARIC Risk Score, PCP-HF) can be useful to estimate subsequent risk of incident HF. PCP-HF provides race- and sex-specific 10-year risk equations using age, blood pressure, fasting glucose, BMI, cholesterol, smoking status, and QRS duration.

source_text: In the general population, validated multivariable risk scores can be useful to estimate subsequent risk of incident HF.

logic_node.action: SGLT2 inhibitors not evaluated in severe renal impairment
logic_node.action_detail: SGLT2 inhibitors have not been evaluated in patients with severe renal impairment (eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73 m2). Use in this population lacks evidence.

source_text: SGLT2i are generally well tolerated, but these agents have not been evaluated in those with severe renal impairment (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] <25 mL/min/1.73 m2).

logic_node.action: Perform echocardiography and refer to cardiovascular specialist
logic_node.action_detail: In patients at risk for HF with BNP levels >=50 pg/mL, echocardiography and referral to a cardiovascular specialist should be performed to evaluate for asymptomatic LV dysfunction (systolic or diastolic). This reduced composite endpoint of asymptomatic LV dysfunction with or without newly diagnosed HF (STOP-HF trial).

source_text: screening with BNP testing and then intervening on those with levels of >= 50 pg/mL (performing echocardiography and referral to a cardiovascular specialist) reduced the composite endpoint of asymptomatic LV dysfunction with or without newly diagnosed HF.
